cells.reason: Read-across cell: the anchor is Regulation (EU) 2023/915 Annex I 3.5.1, inorganic tin 200 mg/kg in 'canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products', product as placed on the market; this product (cephalopods, expressly not canned) is uncanned, so the anchor's product_scope does not cover this form and it is offered only as an analog. It is not the nearest same-basis sovereign instrument: three non-gated content-basis tin rows directly cover uncanned food of this kind, Singapore Food Regulations reg 31(4) 'any food' 250 ppm (sg_foodregs_2026_any_food_sn_250000, in force 2026-01-30), Thailand MoPH Notification 414 'foods other than the listed tin categories' 250 mg/kg (th_moph414_2020_sn_food_other_250000, in force 2020-11-16) and Uruguay RBN 'foods in general except categories with particular limits' 250 mg/kg (uy_rbn_general_sn_foods_250mgkg), so this is not a cell that no government regulates and no read-across is needed; if a canned analog is nevertheless wanted, the fishery-specific canned rows (MX NOM-242 canned fishery products 100 mg/kg, CR RTCR 409 and IN FSSAI canned fish 200 mg/kg) are nearer than the EU general canned-food row. None of the directly applicable rows is stricter than 200000, so the magnitude is protective and I would keep 200000, but only re-tagged as a precautionary value sitting below the 250 mg/kg direct instruments (or anchored to them at 250000 under the government-limit default), not presented as the governing read-across.
